text:
Colorado arrives off a 6-3 win over Tampa Bay on Friday, though it was outplayed in the chances that game (42% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality). The Avalanche are 2-2-1 in their last five and are missing Nicolas Roy and Zachary L'Heureux. Nashville is on the second night of a back-to-back, having lost 3-2 in overtime in Pittsburgh last night, and is 1-2-2 in its last five, outscored 19-11. The game also brings reunions: Jack Drury and Ross Colton face their old Colorado team, and Fedor Svechkov is back in Nashville.

Our numbers favor the Avalanche, who have taken 52% of the five-on-five expected goals this season to Nashville's 43%. We project 3.39 goals for Colorado and 2.59 for Nashville. Colorado's power play creates 0.68 expected goals a game against Nashville's 0.57, and Nashville's penalty kill allows more (0.57 to 0.48). Both backups are projected to start. Scott Wedgewood has been about average this season and was 23.58 goals saved above expected last year. Justus Annunen sits at -1.52 over his one game and was 7.07 last year.

Nathan MacKinnon is 44% to score and 87% for a point, with a four-point night to his name on Friday. Artturi Lehkonen has a six-game point streak, and Martin Necas is 72% for a point. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos leads at 31% to score. Our under-the-radar picks are T.J. Hughes, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous (21% to score), and Nazem Kadri, 58% for a point as his line creates chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
